messages:
kate_sales: Customer (FinArc) — POC next Wed. They require: preserve client source IP for allowlists, SNI inspecting on-prem firewall, fixed egress IPs, and minimal changes on their side. Can we outline recommended connectivity patterns (PrivateLink vs TGW/peering), exact firewall ports, NAT behavior, and any POC pricing caveats? Who can +1?

ajay_netops: quick summary: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) and VPC peering / TGW are the two main patterns. Tradeoffs: latency/ops vs source-IP semantics. Short options: 
1) PrivateLink + customer proxy (least infra on our side) — customer will see traffic from our endpoint IPs/ENIs, not original client IP. If they need original identity, use application-level headers (X-Forwarded-For) or mTLS client certs at their proxy.
2) TGW / VPC Peering (preserves client src IP) — traffic flows from their subnets into our routing domain; more setup and approvals but preserves IPs end-to-end.

ajay_netops: firewall rules (recommended baseline): allow outbound TCP 443 to our service domain/IPs. Ephemeral return ports 1024-65535 need to be allowed for stateful sessions. If they have strict SNI inspection, we recommend mTLS or signed client certs so inspection doesn't break auth.

sam_eng: POC-level SG / proxy snippet below (customer side):
```
# security group that allows outbound to our endpoint
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
Port: 443
Destination: <our-privatelink-dns-or-eip-pool>
# ephemeral ports for replies are implicit for stateful SGs; if using stateless ACL allow 1024-65535 TCP established
```

sam_eng: Notes: if they demand a static EIP list we can provide a small temporary egress pool for the POC (size depends on throughput). That will simplify firewall allowlisting but may increase Dedicated/Private pricing if we reserve EIPs or NAT capacity.

ajay_netops: Important behavioral caveat: PrivateLink creates interface ENIs — the source IPs seen by the customer's firewall will typically be the NAT/Egress IPs owned by our side. So "preserve src IP" is not a characteristic you should assume for PrivateLink. If the customer must see original client IP for logging or policy enforcement, plan on either: (a) moving auth into the app layer (XFF/mTLS), or (b) using TGW/peering where packets originate in their address space.

kate_sales: Customer asks about allowlisting by FQDN vs fixed IPs. What do we recommend for minimal ops?

sam_eng: For minimal ops: FQDN allowlist to our hostname + mTLS is easiest. Many enterprise firewalls support FQDN+SNI rules. If their firewall only supports IP allowlist, ask whether a temporary small EIP pool is acceptable for the POC — we can publish 2-4 IPs.

ajay_netops: Pricing/POC note: PrivateLink has endpoint-hour and data processing charges on AWS; TGW/peering has data transfer model differences. For POC we can do a limited-time complimentary throughput window but Sales should flag any heavy egress for billing.

kate_sales: Action items: (1) @ajay_netops produce a simple diagram of 2 patterns (PrivateLink + TGW) and callouts for src-IP behavior by EOD. (2) @sam_eng add SG snippet & example allowlist text to the POC repo. (3) I'll ask FinArc if they can accept FQDN+mTLS or need static IPs.

ops_bot: Reminder: schedule deploy window => POC slot Wed 10:00-12:00. Please add calendar invite when designs are ready.

ajay_netops: ack — will post diagram in the thread and drop a compact checklist for firewall rules and proxy config (including Proxy Protocol / X-Forwarded-For notes). :thumbsup:
